A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Nostrils: Your nose alternates which side does most of the breathing, switching every few hours in what is called the nasal cycle.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Nasal cavity: Inside, moist tissue warms and humidifies air, and mucus traps dust, so air arrives near body temperature.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Pharynx: Food and air share the throat, a crossroads where a swallow reflex sends each the right way.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Larynx: The voice box holds the vocal folds, and a small flap, the epiglottis, folds over it when you swallow.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Trachea: Held open by C-shaped cartilage rings, the windpipe is lined with tiny hairs that sweep mucus and dust upward.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Main bronchus: The right bronchus is wider and steeper than the left, so inhaled objects more often end up on that side.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Bronchiole: These airways are under a millimeter wide and have no cartilage, only muscle that tightens during an asthma attack.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Alveolar duct: Tiny passages lined with clusters of air sacs, rather like a bunch of grapes on a stem.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Alveolus: Hundreds of millions of these air sacs together give the lungs a gas-exchange surface of tens of square meters.
A breath of air's journey into your bloo.Blood capillary: So narrow that red blood cells pass single file, and oxygen crosses a barrier under a thousandth of a millimeter thick.

Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Summit of Everest: At the top of the world's highest peak, air pressure is only about a third of sea level, so water boils at a temperature too low to cook pasta properly.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Everest Base Camp: Climbers at base camp find that cooking takes much longer, since boiling water here is cooler than at sea level.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Summit of Mont Blanc: Western Europe's highest peak has such thin air that boiling water is noticeably cooler than at home, which is why cooking takes long.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.La Paz: At about 3,600 metres, this Bolivian city is one of the highest capital cities in the world, so cooking takes extra time.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Quito: Ecuador's capital sits at about 2,850 metres in the Andes, so even a kettle boils well below the usual 100 degrees.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Mexico City: Built high on a plateau at about 2,240 metres, this huge city has water boiling noticeably lower than at the coast.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Denver: The Mile High City sits at about 1,600 metres, so recipes and baking often need adjusting for its thinner air.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Any beach at sea level: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius under standard air pressure, the reference point for the Celsius scale.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Dead Sea shore: The Dead Sea shore is the lowest dry land on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level, so the thicker air makes water boil slightly hotter.
Where water boils hottest for your pasta.Inside a pressure cooker: Sealing in steam raises the pressure, which raises the boiling point, so food cooks much faster than in an open pot.

Early British history, in order.Romans invade Britain: Emperor Claudius ordered the invasion, and elephants were reportedly brought along to impress local tribes.
Early British history, in order.Hadrian's Wall begun: Stretching about 118 km coast to coast, it was named for the emperor who visited Britain in 122 and ordered it built.
Early British history, in order.Romans leave Britain: Emperor Honorius is said to have told British cities to defend themselves, as Rome couldn't spare troops.
Early British history, in order.Augustine's mission lands: Sent by Pope Gregory, he became the first Archbishop of Canterbury and converted King Æthelberht of Kent.
Early British history, in order.Vikings raid Lindisfarne: The raid on the island monastery shocked Christian Europe and is often used to mark the start of the Viking Age.
Early British history, in order.Alfred wins at Edington: Alfred the Great defeated the Viking leader Guthrum, who then accepted baptism, and Wessex survived.
Early British history, in order.Battle of Hastings: It was fought at Senlac Hill, near the town of Battle, not Hastings itself. King Harold died there.
Early British history, in order.Magna Carta: King John sealed it at Runnymede, and only a few clauses remain in English law today.
Early British history, in order.Peasants' Revolt: A poll tax sparked it, and Wat Tyler led Kentish rebels into London, where he was killed meeting young Richard II.
Early British history, in order.Battle of Bosworth: Richard III died here, the last English king to die in battle. His body was found under a Leicester car park in 2012.

Heights of giant dams.Aswan High Dam: It created Lake Nasser and forced the relocation of the Abu Simbel temples to higher ground.
Heights of giant dams.Kariba Dam: On the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe, it created one of the world's largest reservoirs by volume.
Heights of giant dams.Tarbela Dam, Pakistan: This dam on the Indus is one of the largest in the world by volume of earth and rock fill.
Heights of giant dams.Grand Coulee Dam: The largest concrete structure in the US, it produces power and irrigates the Columbia basin.
Heights of giant dams.Three Gorges Dam: The world's largest power station by capacity, at 22.5 gigawatts, it displaced over a million people.
Heights of giant dams.Itaipu Dam: Shared by Brazil and Paraguay, it supplies around 90 percent of Paraguay's electricity.
Heights of giant dams.Hoover Dam: Built in the Depression, its concrete was poured in blocks cooled by pipes. Lake Mead lies behind it.
Heights of giant dams.Inguri Dam, Georgia: One of the tallest concrete arch dams in the world, it was built in Soviet times on a river in Georgia.
Heights of giant dams.Grande Dixence, Switzerland: The tallest gravity dam in the world, in the Swiss Alps.
Heights of giant dams.Nurek Dam, Tajikistan: An earth-fill dam on the Vakhsh river, it was the world's tallest dam for decades, until Rogun, also in Tajikistan, topped it.

Sharks from shortest to longest.Dwarf lanternshark: One of the smallest sharks known, it fits in a human hand and has light-producing organs that glow in the dark.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Small-spotted catshark: Its eggs come in leathery cases called mermaid's purses, often found washed up on beaches.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Spiny dogfish: Each dorsal fin has a venomous spine, and females can carry pups for up to two years.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Blacktip reef shark: Often seen in shallow reef waters, it is rarely dangerous to people and can leap clear of the water.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Bull shark: It tolerates freshwater and has been found far up rivers, including the Mississippi and Amazon.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Shortfin mako: One of the fastest sharks, it reaches bursts of around 70 km/h and can leap clear out of the water.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Great white shark: This is the largest predatory fish, and females grow bigger than males.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Basking shark: This gentle giant filters plankton by swimming with its enormous mouth open, ignoring bigger prey.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Whale shark: The largest fish on Earth; its spot pattern is unique to each individual, like a fingerprint.
Sharks from shortest to longest.Megalodon: Known mostly from teeth over 15 cm long, it went extinct a few million years ago, and size estimates vary.

Famous museum treasures, by age.Venus of Willendorf: The limestone figurine, about 11 cm tall, was found in Austria in 1908.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Narmer Palette: It shows the unification of Egypt and bears some of the earliest hieroglyphic inscriptions.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Standard of Ur: The mosaic box from Sumerian royal graves is in the British Museum.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Mask of Agamemnon: Schliemann claimed it was Agamemnon's, but it is about 300 years older than the Trojan War era.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Tutankhamun's gold mask: It holds over 10 kg of solid gold and was found by Howard Carter in 1922.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Rosetta Stone: Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphs; it is inscribed in three scripts.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Sutton Hoo helmet: Found in a ship burial in Suffolk, it probably belonged to King Raedwald of East Anglia.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Bayeux Tapestry: It is actually embroidery, about 70 metres long, telling the story of the Norman conquest.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Lewis Chessmen: Carved from walrus ivory, found on the Isle of Lewis in 1831; some inspired Harry Potter's chess set.
Famous museum treasures, by age.Gutenberg Bible: About 180 copies were printed, and around 49 survive in whole or in part.

Pixel counts of these screens.Nokia 3310: Launched in 2000, its black-and-white screen ran Snake II, and its battery lasted days; it sold over 126 million.
Pixel counts of these screens.TI-83 calculator: Millions of students used it in math class, and it can run games and programs written by users thanks to its Z80 processor.
Pixel counts of these screens.Game Boy: Nintendo's 1989 handheld had a four-shade green screen, and its bundled Tetris helped the Game Boy line sell over 100 million units.
Pixel counts of these screens.Game Boy Advance: Released in 2001, it was the first Game Boy with a 32-bit processor, running games close to Super Nintendo quality.
Pixel counts of these screens.Nintendo DS (each screen): DS stands for dual screen; the bottom one was a touch screen, a new idea for Nintendo's handhelds in 2004.
Pixel counts of these screens.PSP: Sony's 2004 PlayStation Portable played its games and movies from small UMD discs, a format used by almost nothing else.
Pixel counts of these screens.Original iPhone: Its 3.5-inch multitouch screen in 2007 made physical phone keyboards feel old, and it launched with no App Store at all.
Pixel counts of these screens.iPhone 4: Its 2010 Retina display packed 326 pixels per inch, high enough that Apple said the eye could not pick out single pixels at normal distance.
Pixel counts of these screens.Nintendo Switch (handheld): Docked, it sends 1080p video to a TV, but in handheld mode the Switch uses this 6.2-inch 720p screen.
Pixel counts of these screens.iPad Pro 12.9-inch: Its screen holds about 5.6 million pixels, over a thousand times as many as the Nokia 3310's.

Digital payment firsts.First cash machine (ATM): Barclays installed the first one in Enfield, north London, in June 1967, and it initially took paper vouchers.
Digital payment firsts.First barcode scanned: A pack of Wrigley's gum was the first item scanned, at a supermarket in Troy, Ohio.
Digital payment firsts.PayPal launches: It began as Confinity, then merged with Elon Musk's X.com before being sold to eBay in 2002.
Digital payment firsts.M-Pesa: Its name combines M for mobile with pesa, the Swahili word for money, and it transformed finance in Kenya.
Digital payment firsts.Venmo: It started as a text-message-based way to split bills, then added a social feed of payments.
Digital payment firsts.Square card reader: Jim McKelvey lost a glass sale because he could not take a card, which led to this tiny reader.
Digital payment firsts.Google Wallet: It was among the first to use NFC tap-to-pay, and was later merged into Google Pay.
Digital payment firsts.Apple Pay: It uses tokenization, so your actual card number is never shared with the merchant, and it arrived with iPhone 6.
Digital payment firsts.Zelle: A network owned by a group of large US banks that moves money between accounts within minutes.
Digital payment firsts.Pix (Brazil): Brazil's central bank launched this instant system, and it's now used by well over a hundred million people.

Birth years of great architects.Filippo Brunelleschi: He built the Florence cathedral's dome without a wooden centering frame, using a herringbone brick pattern.
Birth years of great architects.Andrea Palladio: His villas and treatises inspired Palladian style, shaping Jefferson's Monticello and countless English country houses.
Birth years of great architects.Christopher Wren: After the 1666 Great Fire he rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral and designed dozens of City of London churches.
Birth years of great architects.Antoni Gaudí: He worked on Barcelona's Sagrada Familia for over 40 years, and it remained unfinished at his death in 1926.
Birth years of great architects.Frank Lloyd Wright: He designed Fallingwater, a house built over a waterfall, and New York's spiralling Guggenheim Museum.
Birth years of great architects.Le Corbusier: Born Charles-Edouard Jeanneret, he took a relative's name as his pen name and called a house a machine for living in.
Birth years of great architects.I. M. Pei: He designed the Louvre's glass pyramid and Hong Kong's Bank of China Tower, winning the Pritzker Prize in 1983.
Birth years of great architects.Frank Gehry: Known for crumpled metal forms, he designed Bilbao's Guggenheim and Walt Disney Concert Hall using aircraft-design software.
Birth years of great architects.Norman Foster: He designed London's Gherkin and the glass dome of the Reichstag, and won the Pritzker Prize in 1999.
Birth years of great architects.Zaha Hadid: In 2004 she became the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, and was nicknamed Queen of the Curve.

How much these foods weigh.Grain of rice: This tiny grain is the daily staple for roughly half of humanity, and a single rice plant produces hundreds of them on its seed heads.
How much these foods weigh.Roasted coffee bean: Each bean is the seed of a cherry-like fruit, and a typical cup of coffee uses around 70 beans, which means that it adds up quickly.
How much these foods weigh.Grape: Grapes are among the oldest cultivated fruits, with wine-making traces of over 7,000 years in the Caucasus, and a raisin is just a dried one.
How much these foods weigh.Chicken egg: The egg's shell has about 7,000 to 17,000 tiny pores, and a fresh egg sinks in water while an older one floats because of the air that enters.
How much these foods weigh.Apple: Apples float in water because about a quarter of their volume is air, and the fruit originated in the mountains of Kazakhstan.
How much these foods weigh.Loaf of bread: Archaeologists found charred flatbread baked in Jordan about 14,400 years ago, thousands of years before farming began, so bread is far older than agriculture.
How much these foods weigh.Wheel of Brie: Brie de Meaux, the classic wheel, is edible from rind to center, and the bloomy white rind is a mold, Penicillium candidum, added on purpose.
How much these foods weigh.Thanksgiving turkey: Americans eat roughly 45 million of these around Thanksgiving, and the wild ancestors can fly in short bursts, unlike the heavy farm birds.
How much these foods weigh.Wheel of Parmigiano: Each wheel needs about 550 liters of milk and ripens for at least 12 months, and Italian banks accept the wheels as loan collateral.
How much these foods weigh.Adult bluefin tuna: A giant bluefin can swim at speeds up to 70 km/h, and a single fish has sold at a Tokyo auction for over 3 million dollars.

1,729 is the 'taxicab number': Ramanujan said it is the smallest number that is the sum of two cubes in two different ways.
Famous enormous numbers.Kaprekar's constant: Kaprekar's constant, 6,174, has a strange property: repeat a certain rearranging and subtracting process on any four-digit number, and you end up at it.
Famous enormous numbers.8th Mersenne prime: 2,147,483,647 is the eighth Mersenne prime, and it is the largest value of a signed 32-bit integer in computing.
Famous enormous numbers.Rice on a doubling chessboard: Legend says the inventor of chess asked for a grain of rice on the first square, doubling on every square, which would give over 18 quintillion grains.
Famous enormous numbers.Avogadro's number: Avogadro's number is the number of particles in a mole, which makes it possible to count atoms by weighing a substance.
Famous enormous numbers.Order of the Monster group: The Monster group is the biggest of the sporadic simple groups, and mathematicians discovered it in a surprising link with 'monstrous moonshine'.
Famous enormous numbers.Atoms in observable universe: There are about 10^80 atoms in the observable universe, which is a tiny fraction of a googol.
Famous enormous numbers.Googol: A googol, coined by a nine-year-old nephew of a mathematician, inspired the name of Google, which was spelled differently by accident.
Famous enormous numbers.Centillion (short scale): A centillion is 1 followed by 303 zeros in the short scale, and it is a number that the English language names but few ever need.
Famous enormous numbers.Googolplex: A googolplex is 10 raised to a googol, which is so big that you could not write it out even if every atom in the universe held a digit.

When these Apple products came out.Apple II: Designed by Steve Wozniak, it was one of the first mass-produced personal computers and offered color graphics.
When these Apple products came out.Macintosh: It was introduced by the 1984 Super Bowl ad directed by Ridley Scott.
When these Apple products came out.Macintosh Portable: It weighed about 7 kg, which made calling it portable quite a stretch.
When these Apple products came out.iMac: Its translucent Bondi-blue case and lack of a floppy drive made it a design landmark by Jony Ive.
When these Apple products came out.iPod: Apple pitched it as 1,000 songs in your pocket.
When these Apple products came out.iPhone: Steve Jobs introduced it in 2007 as three devices in one: an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator.
When these Apple products came out.MacBook Air: Steve Jobs pulled it out of a manila envelope on stage to show how thin it was.
When these Apple products came out.iPad: It sold about 3 million in its first 80 days, despite jokes about its name.
When these Apple products came out.Apple Watch: It was Apple's first new product category after Steve Jobs died.
When these Apple products came out.Vision Pro: Apple calls it a spatial computer, and it launched at $3,499.

English kings from the Norman Conquest o.William the Conqueror: He was crowned on Christmas Day 1066 and ordered the Domesday Book survey in 1086.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.William Rufus: Red-haired, he died by an arrow in the New Forest in 1100, and whether it was an accident or murder is debated.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Henry I: He had over 20 illegitimate children, but his only legitimate son drowned in the White Ship disaster of 1120.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Stephen: His reign was dominated by the Anarchy, a civil war against his cousin Matilda.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Henry II: He founded the Plantagenet dynasty, and Thomas Becket was killed in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170 after the king's angry words.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Richard the Lionheart: Captured on his way home from the Crusade, he was held for ransom by the Holy Roman Emperor.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.King John: He sealed Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215, and legend says he lost his jewels in the Wash.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Henry III: With a 56-year reign, he ruled for one of the longest periods of any English king and rebuilt Westminster Abbey.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Edward Longshanks: Nicknamed for his long legs, he stood about 6 feet 2 inches, conquered Wales and was called Hammer of the Scots.
English kings from the Norman Conquest o.Edward II: The first English heir to hold the title Prince of Wales, he was deposed in 1327 by his wife Isabella and Roger Mortimer.

The life of Napoleon, in order.Born in Corsica: Corsica had become French only the year before his birth, after being sold by Genoa.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Siege of Toulon: His artillery plan won back the port from British forces and made him a general at 24.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Egyptian campaign: He brought over 150 scholars, and his soldiers found the Rosetta Stone in 1799.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Crowned emperor: He took the crown from the Pope and placed it on his own head.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Battle of Austerlitz: Fought against Russia and Austria, it is considered his greatest victory.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Invades Russia: His Grande Armée of over 600,000 men set out, and only a fraction came home.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Exiled to Elba: He escaped after less than a year and returned to France with about a thousand men.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Battle of Waterloo: He was beaten by Wellington and Blücher, ending the Hundred Days.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Dies on St. Helena: He died on a remote South Atlantic island, and the cause of death is still debated.
The life of Napoleon, in order.Reburied at Les Invalides: His remains returned to France and rest in a giant red porphyry tomb.

The decade each fashion trend peaked.Crinoline skirts: Cage-like hooped petticoats made huge skirts possible and sometimes caused accidents.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Bustles: Padding at the back of skirts created a dramatic silhouette.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Flapper dresses: Loose dresses and bobbed hair symbolized freedom in the Jazz Age.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Zoot suits: The baggy suits became a symbol of rebellion, and sparked the 1943 Zoot Suit Riots in Los Angeles.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Poodle skirts: Felt circle skirts with appliqué decorations were a teen staple of the decade.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Miniskirts: Mary Quant helped popularize them and reportedly named them after her favorite car, the Mini.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Bell-bottoms: Flared trousers have a naval origin, since sailors found them easy to roll up.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Power shoulder pads: Padded shoulders conveyed authority in TV shows like Dynasty and in 'power suits'.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Grunge flannel shirts: Marc Jacobs' 1992 grunge collection for Perry Ellis got him fired.
The decade each fashion trend peaked.Low-rise jeans: Alexander McQueen's 'bumsters' in the 1990s pushed hemlines low, and the style later went mainstream.

Fill in the number: bigger idioms.The ___-year itch: Billy Wilder's 1955 comedy made the phrase famous, with Marilyn Monroe's white dress billowing over a subway grate in its best-known scene.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.A cat has ___ lives: The idea of cats having several lives is old, but in Arabic and Spanish-speaking cultures the number is seven, not nine.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.A dime a ___: The word dozen comes from Old French for "twelve". It stuck because twelve divides neatly by 2, 3, 4 and 6, which ten does not.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.A baker's ___: The extra loaf is often traced to medieval English bread laws that fined bakers for short-weight loaves, so they added one to be safe.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.Sweet ___: In the United States this birthday is a classic milestone party, and in many states it is the age when teens can get a driver's license.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.Talk ___ to the dozen: This British phrase for rapid chatter dates back to at least the 1700s. The number is just for effect, since nineteen is more than twelve.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.Catch-___: Joseph Heller's 1961 novel gave English this phrase for a no-win rule. It was nearly titled Catch-18, until another book with an 18 in the title appeared.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.___ winks: Here "wink" is an old word for a nap. The phrase for a short sleep was popularized in the early 1800s.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.A picture is worth ___ words: The saying is often credited to an advertising man who used it in a 1921 trade ad and attributed it to a "Chinese proverb" to add weight.
Fill in the number: bigger idioms.The ___-dollar question: The big question that decides everything. Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? began in Britain in 1998 and was sold to dozens of countries.

Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Denny's: Started in Lakewood, California, as "Danny's Donuts", it was renamed in 1959. It's known as a 24-hour diner, and its Grand Slam breakfast is famous.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Waffle House: Founded in Avondale Estates, Georgia, it hardly ever closes, so FEMA's informal "Waffle House Index" uses its closures to judge hurricane damage.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.IHOP: The International House of Pancakes began in Los Angeles in 1958. It rebranded in 2018 as "IHOb" for a joke, announcing its new burgers.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.TGI Fridays: Opened in New York's Upper East Side in 1965, it's known for its red-and-white striped awnings and "flair" bartenders, and it's said to have helped popularize the singles bar.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Red Lobster: Started in Lakeland, Florida, in 1968, it is a chain famous for its Cheddar Bay Biscuits and for seafood served in a casual setting.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Hard Rock Cafe: Founded by Isaac Tigrett and Peter Morton in London, it displays rock memorabilia, starting with Eric Clapton's guitar.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.The Cheesecake Factory: Founded by David Overton, it offers a menu of over 250 items, and its cheesecakes come in dozens of flavors.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Applebee's: Its first restaurant opened in Atlanta in 1980 as "T.J. Applebee's Rx for Edibles & Elixirs" before the name was shortened and it grew into a giant.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Olive Garden: The Italian-themed chain from Darden began in Orlando in 1982, and is known for its "When you're here, you're family" slogan and unlimited breadsticks.
Sit-down restaurant chains, by founding.Outback Steakhouse: Despite its Australian theme, the chain was founded in Tampa, Florida. Its Bloomin' Onion appetizer is American, not Australian.

Age at death: who lived longest?.Jimi Hendrix: The guitar legend died in London in 1970 at 27, joining the "27 Club" of artists who died that young, including Janis Joplin and Kurt Cobain.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart: The composer died in Vienna in 1791 while writing his Requiem, leaving it unfinished, after writing over 600 works in his short life.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Marilyn Monroe: Born Norma Jeane Mortenson, she died in 1962. Andy Warhol's silkscreen portraits of her, made just after her death, helped define pop art.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Elvis Presley: The "King of Rock and Roll" died in 1977 at Graceland, his Memphis home. His first hit single was "Heartbreak Hotel" in 1956.
Age at death: who lived longest?.John F. Kennedy: The 35th US president was assassinated in Dallas in 1963, and he was the youngest man elected president, at age 43.
Age at death: who lived longest?.William Shakespeare: The English playwright died in 1616 in Stratford-upon-Avon, reportedly on his birthday, April 23, according to tradition.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Albert Einstein: The physicist, who developed the theory of relativity, died in 1955 in Princeton, and his brain was preserved by the pathologist who did the autopsy.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Winston Churchill: Britain's wartime prime minister died in 1965 at 90, having led the country through World War II and won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Pablo Picasso: The Spanish painter, co-founder of Cubism, died in 1973 at 91, and produced an estimated 50,000 works over his long career.
Age at death: who lived longest?.Queen Elizabeth II: Britain's longest-reigning monarch died in 2022 at 96, after reigning for 70 years, and was succeeded by her son, Charles III.

Better known as Sonnet 18, it ends by boasting that the poem will keep its subject alive as long as people can read.
Andrew Marvell's 'To His Coy Mistress' was published after his death, and gave us the image of 'Time's winged chariot'.
Famous poems, by their first lines.Tyger Tyger, burning bright: William Blake printed the poem and hand-coloured the plates himself, asking what creator would dare make such a fearsome animal.
Famous poems, by their first lines.I wandered lonely as a cloud: Better known as 'Daffodils', it drew on his sister Dorothy's journal of a walk by Ullswater.
Famous poems, by their first lines.Thou still unravish'd bride: Keats's 'Ode on a Grecian Urn' ends with the line 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty', one of the most debated in English.
Better known as 'Because I could not stop for Death', it appeared in print only after Dickinson died. Almost all her poems were unpublished in her lifetime.
Famous poems, by their first lines.So much depends upon: 'The Red Wheelbarrow' has just sixteen words, and is among the best-known examples of American modernist, imagist verse.
The Welsh poet wrote it for his dying father, using the strict villanelle form, with its two refrains repeating throughout.
Famous poems, by their first lines.Not waving but drowning: Stevie Smith's poem tells of a man whose distress is mistaken for cheerful waving, and its title has become a common phrase.
Better known as 'Still I Rise', it comes from Maya Angelou's 1978 collection And Still I Rise.

Oldest on record.Flopsy the rabbit: This rabbit lived for nearly 19 years, which is around twice the typical age of a pet rabbit, and he appeared in the Guinness book.
Oldest on record.Bluey the dog: The Australian cattle dog is believed to have lived for 29 years, and it is the oldest dog ever verified, working on a farm.
Oldest on record.Creme Puff the cat: This Texas cat lived to 38 years, and her owner had a number of cats that lived for over 30 years.
Oldest on record.Tish the goldfish: The goldfish lived for 43 years, and he won a prize for being the oldest at a fair in England, and the owners were a couple.
Oldest on record.Old Billy the horse: The English horse lived for 62 years, and he pulled barges along canals, and the old horse's skull is preserved in a museum.
Oldest on record.Cookie the cockatoo: The Major Mitchell's cockatoo lived for 83 years, and he spent most of his life at Brookfield Zoo near Chicago.
Oldest on record.Jeanne Calment: The French woman is the oldest verified human, and she once met Vincent van Gogh as a girl in her father's shop.
Oldest on record.Tu'i Malila the tortoise: This radiated tortoise was given to the royal family of Tonga by Captain Cook, and it died in 1965.
Oldest on record.Ming the clam: An ocean quahog clam was dredged from Iceland's waters, and scientists accidentally killed it while counting its growth rings.
Oldest on record.Methuselah the pine tree: This bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains is among the oldest known individual trees, and its location is kept secret.

James Bond theme songs, in order.The James Bond Theme: Credited to Monty Norman but arranged by John Barry, whose twangy guitar riff, played by Vic Flick, made the tune instantly spy-like.
James Bond theme songs, in order.Goldfinger: Shirley Bassey belted it with such force that she became the voice of Bond, returning for two more themes in later films.
James Bond theme songs, in order.Live and Let Die: Paul McCartney and Wings made the first rock-era Bond theme, and it earned an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song.
James Bond theme songs, in order.Nobody Does It Better: Carly Simon sang it for The Spy Who Loved Me; its title never mentions the film, and Marvin Hamlisch co-wrote the music.
James Bond theme songs, in order.A View to a Kill: Duran Duran took this theme to number one in the US, the only Bond theme to top the Billboard Hot 100.
James Bond theme songs, in order.GoldenEye: Tina Turner sang this theme, written for her by Bono and The Edge of U2, to launch Pierce Brosnan's first Bond film.
James Bond theme songs, in order.You Know My Name: Chris Cornell's rock theme opened Daniel Craig's debut in Casino Royale, and it was the first Bond song title not shared with its film in years.
James Bond theme songs, in order.Skyfall: Adele's song won the Oscar for Best Original Song, the first Bond theme to take the prize.
James Bond theme songs, in order.Writing's on the Wall: Sam Smith's ballad for Spectre also won the Oscar, giving Bond back-to-back winners within a few years.
James Bond theme songs, in order.No Time to Die: Billie Eilish wrote it with her brother Finneas when she was 18, and it won her an Oscar and a Grammy.

The 10th term of each sequence.Odd numbers (1, 3, 5…): The sum of the first ten odd numbers is 100, because adding odd numbers in order always gives a perfect square.
The 10th term of each sequence.Even numbers (2, 4, 6…): Two is the only even prime, which makes this family of numbers very close to prime-free.
The 10th term of each sequence.Prime numbers: Euclid proved around 300 BC that the primes never run out, and 29 is only the tenth.
The 10th term of each sequence.Fibonacci (1, 1, 2, 3…): Leonardo of Pisa brought the sequence to Europe in 1202, and it shows up in the spirals of sunflowers and pinecones.
The 10th term of each sequence.Square numbers: The name comes from the shape: ancient Greeks arranged pebbles into square grids, and 100 is ten rows of ten.
The 10th term of each sequence.Pentagonal numbers: Euler linked pentagonal numbers to the ways of splitting a number into parts, a surprising bridge between shapes and counting.
The 10th term of each sequence.Tetrahedral numbers: These count cannonballs stacked in a triangular pyramid, and 220 is also half of the smallest amicable pair with 284.
The 10th term of each sequence.Powers of 2 (1, 2, 4…): Each term doubles the last, and 2 to the 10th is 1,024, the reason a kilobyte is not exactly a thousand bytes.
The 10th term of each sequence.Cube numbers: Mathematicians know 1,729 as the smallest number that is a sum of two cubes in two different ways.
The 10th term of each sequence.Factorials (1!, 2!, 3!…): Ten factorial is exactly six weeks measured in seconds, a coincidence that is true and easy to check.

US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Private First Class: Most soldiers reach this rank after about a year, and its insignia is a single chevron with a curved bar beneath.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Specialist: It has the same pay grade as a corporal, but without the same leadership duties.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Sergeant: The first noncommissioned officer rank, often called the backbone of the Army.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Staff Sergeant: This rank commonly leads a squad of soldiers.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Sergeant First Class: Often a platoon sergeant, who advises the officer and trains the soldiers.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Master Sergeant: A rank of two types: a master sergeant holds technical expertise, while first sergeants lead companies.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Sergeant Major: The Sergeant Major of the Army is the top enlisted soldier and advises the Army's chief of staff.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Warrant Officer 1: Warrant officers are specialists, such as helicopter pilots, appointed by warrant rather than commission.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Chief Warrant Officer 5: It is the highest warrant rank, a rank of top technical masters held by only a very few.
US Army ranks, from the ranks to the off.Second Lieutenant: The lowest commissioned rank wears a single gold bar, nicknamed the butter bar.

When these food and drink chains first o.A&W: A&W's root beer stand opened in Lodi, California; the name came from founder Roy Allen and his partner Frank Wright.
When these food and drink chains first o.Krispy Kreme: Founded by Vernon Rudolph in Winston-Salem, North Carolina; its Hot Now sign tells passersby fresh doughnuts are coming off the line.
When these food and drink chains first o.Dairy Queen: Its first store, in Joliet, Illinois, was built around soft-serve ice cream, which was a brand-new idea at the time.
When these food and drink chains first o.Dunkin': It opened as Dunkin' Donuts in Quincy, Massachusetts, and dropped the word Donuts from its name in 2019.
When these food and drink chains first o.KFC (first franchise): Colonel Harland Sanders was a real person, and the first franchise opened in Salt Lake City, Utah, run by Pete Harman.
When these food and drink chains first o.Pizza Hut: Brothers Dan and Frank Carney opened the first one in Wichita, Kansas, with 600 dollars borrowed from their mother.
When these food and drink chains first o.Subway: Fred DeLuca was 17 when he borrowed 1,000 dollars from family friend Peter Buck to start it as Pete's Super Submarines.
When these food and drink chains first o.Starbucks: The first shop, in Seattle's Pike Place Market, sold beans rather than brewed coffee; the name comes from Starbuck in Moby-Dick.
When these food and drink chains first o.Chipotle: Steve Ells founded it in Denver, with a loan from his father; the name is the Spanish form of a smoked, dried jalapeño pepper.
When these food and drink chains first o.Shake Shack: It began as a hot-dog cart in New York's Madison Square Park; the first permanent kiosk opened in 2004.

Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Vostok: Yuri Gagarin's 108-minute flight in Vostok 1 made him the first human in space.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Voskhod: A hastily modified Vostok, it carried three cosmonauts without spacesuits, and Voskhod 2 saw the first spacewalk.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Gemini: Its two-person flights practiced docking, spacewalks and long durations for Apollo's Moon landing.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Soyuz: Flying since 1967, it is the longest-serving crewed design and carried astronauts after the Shuttle retired.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Apollo: Apollo 8 first took humans around the Moon in 1968, and the Earthrise photograph came from it.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Space Shuttle: The first reusable crewed spacecraft flew 135 missions from 1981 to 2011, launching Hubble among others.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Shenzhou: With Yang Liwei's flight aboard Shenzhou 5, China became the third nation to launch humans itself.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.SpaceShipOne: It won the 10 million dollar Ansari X Prize by reaching space twice in two weeks, funded by Paul Allen.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Crew Dragon: The first private spacecraft to carry NASA astronauts, it launched Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the ISS.
Crewed spacecraft by first crewed flight.Starliner: Boeing's first crewed flight left two astronauts on the ISS for months while the capsule returned empty.

Route lengths of famous train journeys.Flåm Railway: The Flåm Railway in Norway drops about 860 meters in just 20 km and is among the steepest standard-gauge lines in the world.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.Glacier Express: Billed as the 'slowest express train in the world', this Swiss route crosses 291 bridges and the Oberalp Pass between Zermatt and St. Moritz.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.Tokaido Shinkansen: Opened in 1964 just before the Tokyo Olympics, this was the world's first high-speed line, and it has carried billions of passengers.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.Beijing–Shanghai high-speed: Opened in 2011, this Chinese line cut the Beijing-Shanghai trip from about ten hours to roughly four and a half.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.South Africa's Blue Train: This luxury train in South Africa runs between Pretoria and Cape Town and offers butler service and fine dining on board.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.Coast Starlight: Amtrak's train runs between Seattle and Los Angeles along the Pacific coast and is named after the Starlight stars of the night sky.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.The Ghan: The Ghan crosses Australia from Adelaide to Darwin, and is named after the Afghan cameleers who helped open up the outback.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.California Zephyr: This Amtrak route climbs the Sierra Nevada and the Rockies between Chicago and the San Francisco Bay Area, among America's most scenic rides.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.The Canadian: VIA Rail's flagship route crosses Canada between Toronto and Vancouver, rolling through prairies and the Rocky Mountains.
Route lengths of famous train journeys.Trans-Siberian to Vladivostok: The Trans-Siberian line is the world's longest railway, crossing seven time zones from Moscow to the Pacific coast at Vladivostok.

Deep-space probes by launch year.Pioneer 10: Pioneer 10 was the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter, and it carried a plaque showing humankind's location.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Voyager 1: Voyager 1 carries a golden record with sounds and images of Earth, and it's now the most distant human-made object.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Galileo: Galileo was the first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter and dropped a probe into its atmosphere, and it was deliberately crashed into Jupiter in 2003.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Ulysses: Ulysses flew over the Sun's poles, which no probe had done before, and gave the first look at the Sun from above.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Cassini: Cassini orbited Saturn for 13 years and sent the Huygens probe to land on Titan, the only landing in the outer solar system.
Deep-space probes by launch year.MESSENGER: MESSENGER became the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury, and it revealed water ice in permanently shadowed craters.
Deep-space probes by launch year.New Horizons: New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015, revealing a heart-shaped region, and later explored a Kuiper Belt object.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Juno: Juno orbits Jupiter in an unusual path over its poles, and it's solar-powered despite being billions of kilometers from the Sun.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Parker Solar Probe: Parker Solar Probe has flown into the Sun's corona, and it's the fastest human-made object ever.
Deep-space probes by launch year.Europa Clipper: Europa Clipper will study Jupiter's moon Europa, which has a hidden ocean that might hold conditions suitable for life.

How far from the target.Darts throw line: Darts players stand 2.37 meters from the board, and the board's number order was designed to punish inaccurate throws.
How far from the target.Basketball free throw: The 4.6 meter line is the same in all the major basketball leagues, and the shot is the only one nobody can block.
How far from the target.NBA three-point line (top): The NBA's three-point line is 7.24 meters at the top, and it is shorter, 6.7 meters, in the corners.
How far from the target.Soccer penalty spot: The penalty spot is 11 meters or 12 yards from the goal, and its distance was set in the 1890s.
How far from the target.Horseshoes, stake to stake: In horseshoes, stakes stand 40 feet apart, and a 'ringer' where the shoe encircles the stake scores three points.
How far from the target.Field hockey shooting circle: The shooting circle's arc has a 14.63 meter radius, and a field hockey goal can only be scored from inside it.
How far from the target.Pitcher's rubber to home: The pitching distance, 60 feet 6 inches, came from a typo or mismeasurement in the 1890s, and it stuck.
How far from the target.Cricket, wicket to wicket: A cricket pitch is 22 yards, or one chain, long, a measurement from the surveyor's tool Gunter's chain.
How far from the target.Home plate to first base: Baseball's bases are 90 feet apart, and the distance is carefully calibrated so close plays are decided by inches.
How far from the target.Olympic archery target: At 70 meters, Olympic archers aim at a target that is 122 centimeters wide, but the gold circle is the size of a saucer.

How many possibilities?.Rolling two dice: The most common total is seven, with six ways to make it, while 2 and 12 have just one.
How many possibilities?.Flipping ten coins: This is 2 to the 10th power, and there is only one sequence that gives all heads.
How many possibilities?.Tic-tac-toe games: Perfect play always ends in a draw, which is why children eventually stop playing it with adults.
How many possibilities?.Lotto 6/49 combinations: The odds of matching all six numbers are about one in 14 million.
How many possibilities?.Connect Four positions: The game was solved in 1988: with perfect play, the first player wins.
How many possibilities?.Rubik's Cube states: Despite the size, any cube position can be solved in 20 moves or fewer, a limit nicknamed God's Number.
How many possibilities?.Valid Sudoku grids: This drops to about 5.5 billion once rotations and reflections are treated as the same.
How many possibilities?.Orders of a shuffled deck: A well-shuffled deck is almost certainly in an order that has never occurred before in history.
How many possibilities?.Chess games (Shannon): Claude Shannon made this estimate in 1950, far more than the roughly 10^80 atoms in the observable universe.
How many possibilities?.Go board positions: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016 on this board, a win experts had thought was a decade away.

Woods by hardness (Janka).Balsa: Though botanically a hardwood, it is so light that it built the Kon-Tiki raft in 1947 and countless model planes.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Eastern white pine: Its tall, straight trunks were prized as ship masts, and colonial New England trees were marked with the King's Broad Arrow for the Royal Navy.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Douglas fir: Not a true fir, it honours botanist David Douglas; coastal trees can top 90 metres, among the tallest on Earth.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Black cherry: Its heartwood darkens to a rich reddish brown with age and light, which is why furniture makers love it.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Red oak: Its pores are so open that you can blow air through the length of a short stick, a classic way to tell it from white oak.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Hard maple: Also called sugar maple, it gives us both syrup from its sap and the hard floors of bowling lanes and basketball courts.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Hickory: Its toughness and shock resistance made it the traditional wood for axe and hammer handles, and its smoke flavours barbecue.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Jatoba: Often sold as Brazilian cherry, this South American tree yields flooring that starts pale orange and deepens to a rich red.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Ipe: So dense that it sinks in water, it is used for boardwalks and decks that last decades without rotting.
Woods by hardness (Janka).Lignum vitae: Latin for 'wood of life', it is dense enough to sink and naturally oily, so it was used for ship propeller-shaft bearings.

Collins Words of the Year, in order.Binge-watch: Collins said use of the term jumped about 200% in a year, as streaming services made marathon viewing normal.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Brexit: A blend of Britain and exit, it rose by about 3,400% in use, according to Collins.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Fake news: Collins said use of the phrase rose by about 365% after it was taken up by politicians and media worldwide.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Single-use: Collins said use of the word went up fourfold in a year amid concern about plastic waste.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Climate strike: Inspired by Greta Thunberg's school strikes, the phrase's use rose about a hundredfold, according to Collins.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Lockdown: Before 2020 it was mainly a prison term, but the word came to describe life under pandemic restrictions.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.NFT: Short for non-fungible token; 'fungible' means interchangeable, so the word means a one-of-a-kind digital item.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Permacrisis: Blending 'permanent' and 'crisis', it describes an extended period of instability and insecurity.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.AI: Collins reported use of the term soared in 2023 as chatbots and generative tools reached millions of people.
Collins Words of the Year, in order.Brat: Charli XCX's album gave its name to a lime-green, confident, hedonistic attitude, as Collins put it.

Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Lesser mouse-deer: The lesser mouse-deer is among the smallest hoofed mammals, and it's about the size of a rabbit.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Kirk's dik-dik: Kirk's dik-dik is a tiny antelope named for its alarm call, and pairs mate for life.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Klipspringer: The klipspringer walks on the tips of its hooves, and it lives on rocky outcrops in Africa.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Impala: Impalas can leap about 10 m in a single jump, and they do so to confuse predators.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Red deer stag: Red deer stags roar during the rut, and their antlers fall off and regrow each year.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Plains zebra: Plains zebras' stripes are unique to each individual, and may help deter biting flies.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Moose: Moose are the largest deer, and they are excellent swimmers who can dive for plants.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Giraffe: Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as humans, just seven, and each is hugely elongated.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.White rhino: White rhinos are not white, and the name probably comes from a mistranslated Afrikaans word for wide, describing their mouth.
Plant-eaters, from tiny to colossal.Asian elephant: Asian elephants are smaller than African ones, and they have smaller ears and a domed head.

Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Ben Nevis: The highest peak in the British Isles. Its summit is cloudy most days, and a weather observatory worked there until 1904.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Mount Olympus (Greece): Home of the Greek gods, first climbed in 1913.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Mount Fuji: An active volcano that last erupted in 1707 and has long been a sacred symbol in Japan.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Mont Blanc: Its height changes as its snowcap shifts, and France and Italy dispute exactly where the border lies.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Mount Sharp (Mars): Curiosity has been climbing its layered sediments in Gale Crater, reading Martian history in the rock.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Aconcagua: The tallest peak outside Asia, in Argentina's Andes.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Mount Everest: Named for Surveyor General George Everest. The Tibetan name is Chomolungma.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Maxwell Montes (Venus): The tallest peak on Venus, and the only major feature there named after a man, physicist James Clerk Maxwell.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Boösaule Montes (Io): A peak on Jupiter's volcanic moon Io, taller than Everest.
Mountains of Earth and beyond by height.Olympus Mons (Mars): The largest known volcano in the solar system, about three times the height of Everest.

Manga series, by debut year.Astro Boy: Osamu Tezuka's robot-boy tale, known in Japan as Tetsuwan Atom, became Japan's first hit animated TV series in 1963.
Manga series, by debut year.Doraemon: The robot cat from the 22nd century has no ears because, in the story, a mouse gnawed them off.
Manga series, by debut year.Akira: Katsuhiro Otomo's cyberpunk epic is set in a Neo-Tokyo of 2019; its 1988 film helped introduce anime to Western audiences.
Manga series, by debut year.Dragon Ball: Akira Toriyama loosely based it on the Chinese classic Journey to the West; the hero Goku shares its monkey king's staff and cloud.
Manga series, by debut year.Sailor Moon: Naoko Takeuchi's series defined the magical-girl genre; she is married to Yoshihiro Togashi, creator of Hunter x Hunter.
Manga series, by debut year.One Piece: The best-selling manga series of all time, Eiichiro Oda's pirate saga has sold over 500 million copies.
Manga series, by debut year.Naruto: Masashi Kishimoto's ninja saga ran 700 chapters in Weekly Shonen Jump until 2014, selling over 250 million volumes.
Manga series, by debut year.Death Note: A student finds a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it; its death god Ryuk is famously fond of apples.
Manga series, by debut year.Attack on Titan: Hajime Isayama began it in his early twenties, and it ended in 2021 after 34 volumes, with a finale that sparked years of debate.
Manga series, by debut year.Demon Slayer: Its 2020 film Mugen Train became Japan's highest-grossing film ever, passing Spirited Away.

Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Council of Nicaea: The council set rules for the date: broadly, the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring equinox.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Easter hare first written: German physician Georg Franck von Franckenau wrote about the Easter hare who lays coloured eggs, a tradition from Germany.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Easter Island named: Dutch explorer Jacob Roggeveen arrived on Easter Sunday; locals call it Rapa Nui, and it is famed for its moai statues.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Fry's chocolate egg: The Bristol firm made the first modern chocolate Easter egg in Britain, and it was solid.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Cadbury's chocolate eggs: Cadbury's first Easter eggs had dark chocolate shells filled with sugared almonds.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.White House Egg Roll: President Hayes invited children to roll eggs on the lawn after Congress banned them from Capitol grounds.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.First Fabergé egg: Tsar Alexander III commissioned an egg for his wife; it opens to reveal a golden yolk and a hen.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Easter Parade film: Fred Astaire came out of retirement to replace the injured Gene Kelly, and Judy Garland co-starred.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Peeps chicks: The first Peeps were made by hand with a pastry tube, and each took about 27 hours to make.
Easter, from Nicaea to Peeps.Cadbury Mini Eggs: Their crisp candy shells and seasonal limits have made these speckled eggs a favourite with a loyal following.
